messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: streaming-response tail latency p99 spike detected on prod-west (svc: streaming-proxy). p95=420ms -> 1.6s, p99=1.8s -> 8.9s, error rate (5m)=1.2% :rotating_light:
Ela (oncall): seeing the page, pulling up dashboards now. any customer reports?
Sam C: I just got a webhook failure from payments-app about stalled SSE connections (~30% of requests hanging >10s).
Kevin Ops: Logs show a bunch of proxy upstream timeouts to the worker pool around 3189991008. Possible slow consumers/backpressure.
Maria S: Metrics: connection_count steady, but socket_drop increased, and socket-send-queue depth on streaming-proxy host sp-07 is high.
Ela (oncall): can we pin to specific hosts? tagging sp-07. Sam, can you check worker KV cache pressure?
Sam C: checking kvcache metrics — small spike in cache miss rate and higher mem usage on workers-12/13 starting 3189990950. might be memory GC pauses.
Kevin Ops: ssh'ed into sp-07: iostat looks normal, but Nginx upstream backlog is growing: "upstream queue length: 98".
ops-bot: NOTE: paging escalation to infra@team (threshold reached).
Ela (oncall): @Kevin Ops, do a graceful restart of streaming-proxy on sp-07. @Sam C, please confirm fallback routing to non-streaming endpoints (long-poll) is available and canary it.
Kevin Ops: rolling restart sp-07 now (```sudo systemctl restart streaming-proxy && sleep 3 && tail -n 200 /var/log/streaming-proxy.log | sed -n '1,80p'```), will watch for connection ramp.
Sam C: fallback route exists: route rule streaming->polling-fallback v2. Enabling canary for 5% of traffic from prod-west now.
Maria S: customer impact estimate: ~2% of active streaming sessions affected in the interval, main impact: degraded tail latency, some clients reconnected. No data loss reported.
Ryan (product): flagged for CS. any high-value customers on prod-west?
Ela (oncall): CC @Ryan product and @Sam, prioritize customers with active sessions >100k/min.
Sam C: canary enabled at 3189991320 for 5%. observing reduced p99 for the canary traffic (p99 ~600ms).
Kevin Ops: sp-07 restart complete at 3189991402. logs show repeated "write to client EPIPE" and "client read timeout" prior to restart. snippet:
```
[3189990999] streaming-proxy: WARN client_write_queue=124 conn_id=0x7fae3a write_timeout=30000
[3189991001] worker-12: INFO garbage_collect duration=420ms heap=1.8GB
[3189991015] streaming-proxy: ERROR upstream_timeout id=abcd1234 status=504
```
Ela (oncall): sounds like slow consumers causing backlog which amplified GC on workers. immediate mitigations: 1) keep sp-07 restarted 2) increase proxy upstream timeout to avoid long-held connections? 3) enable per-connection write buffer trimming 4) scale worker pool by +2 temporarily. Thoughts?
Kevin Ops: I increased proxy upstream timeout from 30s -> 10s (shorter) on sp-07 canary so hung connections die faster. also toggled streaming-proxy option to drop clients whose send-queue > 80.
Sam C: scaled worker pool +2 starting 3189991500 on prod-west. also applied a GC tuning flag to workers to reduce stop-the-world pauses: -XX:+UseG1GC +XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=35 (will monitor).
Maria S: p95/p99 after mitigations at 3189991620: p95=220ms, p99=790ms, error rate back to 0.15%. socket queue depths trending down.
Ela (oncall): good. ask ops to watch for recurrence for 30m and keep canary active. @Ryan, please prepare a customer note saying we observed transient streaming stalls, mitigated with proxy and worker changes, no data loss.
Ryan (product): drafting note. will include impact window (3189990900-3189991600) and mitigation steps.
Kevin Ops: followup: we should consider adding per-connection backpressure signals to clients, and a server-side knob to reject slow subscribers earlier. filing infra ticket INF-772 to track long-term fix.
Sam C: also a task to add a streaming-slo alert for 5m p99 > 1.5s for prod-west specifically. hitting global thresholds hides region-specific issues.
Maria S: re-run of repro with synthetic slow consumer shows queue growth within ~30s — will add automated test for stubborn-consumer scenario.
Ela (oncall): handoff to oncall-next in 20m. summary for next oncall: root cause likely slow consumer + worker GC amplified by buffering in streaming-proxy -> increased upstream timeouts and p99 spike. mitigations done: sp-07 restart, proxy drop-on-large-queue, upstream timeout shortened, worker pool scaled +2, GC tuning, 5% fallback canary to long-poll. monitor 30m.
ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: handoff scheduled to next oncall at 3189992910.
Ela (oncall): leaving notes in the incident board, will follow up on INF-772 and alert tuning tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Sam C: +1, will check worker GC graphs in the morning and correlate with heap dumps.
Kevin Ops: leaving a small runbook addition: if streaming p99 > 2s in region, do: 1) enable polling fallback canary 2) restart streaming-proxy hosts with high queue 3) scale workers 4) shorten upstream timeout 5) file INF ticket.
Maria S: logging snapshot archived: https://logs.internal/redwood/prod-west/3189991111 (access: infra).
Ryan (product): customer note ready to send after review.
Ela (oncall): thanks all — monitoring.
